name: CD74HC4067M96
title: High-speed CMOS 16-channel analog multiplexer/demultiplexer
summary: CD74HC4067 and CD74HCT4067 are single-pole sixteen-throw CMOS analog switches: four address inputs S0 to S3 pick which of the channel terminals I0 to I15 joins the common terminal, and an active-low enable E opens all switches when high. Signals pass both ways, so the part serves as a 16:1 multiplexer or a 1:16 demultiplexer for signals between GND and VCC. The HC version runs from 2 V to 6 V; the HCT version runs from 4.5 V to 5.5 V with LSTTL-compatible inputs. Both are specified from -55 °C to +125 °C.

circuits.title: Frequency response test circuit
circuits.description: A signal VIS is coupled through 0.1 µF into a closed channel. The common terminal output VOS is loaded by 50 Ω returned to VCC/2 and 10 pF to ground, and a dB meter reads it against ground.
notes: The switch is on; any channel terminal may take the place of I0.

circuits.title: Sine wave distortion test circuit
circuits.description: A sine wave VIS of 1 kHz to 10 kHz is coupled through 10 µF into a closed channel. The output VOS is loaded by 10 kΩ to VCC/2 and 50 pF to ground and read by a distortion meter.
notes: The switch is on; any channel terminal may take the place of I0.

circuits.title: Control-to-switch feedthrough noise test circuit
circuits.description: The switch is toggled on and off by its control at fCONT = 1 MHz, 50 % duty, with edges of 6 ns or less. The channel input is returned to ground through 600 Ω; the output VOS is loaded by 600 Ω to VCC/2 and 10 pF to ground, and a scope shows the noise the control edges couple into it.
notes: Any channel terminal may take the place of I0; the control drive is a 1 MHz square wave with tr, tf ≤ 6ns.

circuits.title: Switch off signal feedthrough test circuit
circuits.description: With the switch held off (control at VIL), a sine wave VIS of 1 MHz or more is coupled through 0.1 µF onto the channel input, which is terminated by R = 50 Ω to VCC/2. The output VOS is loaded by R = 50 Ω to VCC/2 and C = 10 pF to ground, and a dB meter reads what leaks across the open switch.
notes: VC = VIL. Any channel terminal may take the place of I0.

operation.text: S3 to S0 form a 4-bit binary channel number, S0 the lowest bit. With E low, the switch of that channel closes between its terminal In and COMMON and the other fifteen stay open.
E is active low. A high level on E opens all sixteen switches whatever the address inputs hold.

Each switch conducts either way, so COMMON can be the input with the sixteen channels as outputs (demultiplexer) or the output with them as inputs (multiplexer). The analog signal can range anywhere from GND to VCC.

CD74HC4067 runs from 2 V to 6 V with CMOS input thresholds; noise immunity is 30 % of VCC for both levels at VCC = 5 V. CD74HCT4067 runs from 4.5 V to 5.5 V and takes LSTTL levels, VIL 0.8 V max and VIH 2 V min, while drawing at most 1 µA at CMOS levels. An HCT input held at VCC - 2.1 V draws extra supply current, set by the unit-load figures.
The switching is break-before-make, 6 ns typical at 4.5 V. ON resistance is 70 Ω typical at VCC = 4.5 V and 60 Ω at 6 V.
A binary 1-of-16 decoder drives the switches: five stages lie between the address inputs and each switch, four between the enable and each switch. Each switch is a P and N transistor pair.
Over the temperature range a standard output drives 10 LSTTL loads and a bus-driver output 15.
Typical jobs: gating signals; modulating and demodulating; squelch; chopping; commutation; A/D and D/A conversion; setting frequency, impedance, phase or analog gain under digital control.
